title: नेपाली धातुमा संस्कृत धातुको प्रभाव {Influence of Sanskrit dhatu on Nepali dhatu}
nepali: प्रस्तुत लेखमा नेपाली धातुरचनाको संस्कृतस्रोत (तत्सम एवम् तद्भव) बाट नेपाली भाषामा कति धातु प्रयोग हुन आएकारहेछन् ? यस्ता धातुहरू केके रहेछन् भन्ने विषयलाई उठान गरिएको छ । यस क्रममा मुख्यतः नेपाली धातु रचनामा संस्कृतधातुहरूको प्रभाव, संस्कृत र नेपाली धातुमा रहेका समानता तथा असमानतालाई उपस्थापन गरी तिनीहरूबारे विश्लेषण गरेर निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ । यहाँ विषय विश्लेषणको आधार संस्कृतको ‘पाणिनीय धातुपाठ’लाई र नेपालीको चाहिं परम्परागत नेपाली व्याकरणबाट निर्धारित धातुस्वरूप (नु लगाउन मिल्ने धातु) लाई बनाइएको छ । यहाँ यिनै आधारभूमिमा टेकेर तुलनात्मक एवम् वर्णनात्मक विधि–पद्धतिबाट विषय विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । धातुमा विभिन्न प्रत्यय गाँसिएर बन्ने क्रियापदले विभिन्न काल र पक्ष, भाव, वाच्य, ध्रु्रवत्व आदिलाई बताउँछ तसर्थ क्रियाबाट बोध्य अर्थको मूलआधार धातु हो । धातुको यही मूल अर्थमा कालबोधक प्रत्यय थपिँदा कालबोधक क्रिया र भावबोधक प्रत्यय थपिँदा चाहिँ भावबोधक क्रिया बन्दछन् । यसरी नै अन्य क्रियाको संरचना पनि तयार हुन्छ । अतःक्रियाले दिने अर्थ– काल र यसका पक्ष, भाव, वाच्य, ध्रुवत्व आदि मात्रै हुन् । प्रत्ययसँग मिसिनु पूर्वको धातुले निर्धारित अर्थलाई धारण एवम् परिपोषण गर्ने भएकाले धातुको धारण र पोषण अर्थ (धीयतेऽर्थः यस्मिन् स धातुः) सार्थक छ । नेपालीमा प्रयोगरत तत्सम धातुहरूमा खासै समस्या नभए पनि तद्भव धातुहरूमा भने धेरै ठाउँमा संशय देखिन्छ । आंशिक परिवर्तन भएर नेपाली धातु बन्ने क्रममा कतै एउटै संस्कृत धातुबाट अनेकौं तद्भव धातु निर्माण भएको दाबी गरिएको, कतै एउटै संस्कृत धातुबाट एउटामात्र नेपाली धातु बनेको भनिएको, कतै नेपाली धातुको स्वरूपसंग मिल्न खोजेका आधारमा पनि यसको संस्कृत स्रोत यही हो भनेर किट्ने गरिएको लगायतका समानता र निकटता सम्बन्धी विविधता समस्या देखिएका छन् । उदाहरणका रूपमा छाद्, दि, उघार्, दाउ, घुसार्, मिलाउ, चुन्, काट् आदिलाई लिन सकिन्छ । यस्ता धातुमध्ये कतिपयको संस्कृतस्रोत अनुसन्धेय, शङ्कास्पद र विवादित मानिएको छ र पनि यिनीहरूलाई बहुसङ्ख्यकद्वारा तद्भव धातु मान्ने गरिएको छ । नेपालीमा प्रयोग भइरहेका तेस्रो वर्गका धातुहरू अनुकरणमूलका छन्, खनखनाउ, गडगडाउ, थरथराउ, टकटकाउ आदि यसका उदाहरण हुन् । चौथो वर्गका धातु कति आगन्तुक र कति चाहिँ स्रोत पत्ता नलागेका छन्, यिनीहरू मध्येका स्रोत नखुलेका कतिपय धातु प्राकृत र अपभ्रंश स्रोतका हुन् भनी अनुमान गरिएको छ । अटाउ, छाड्, टिक्, ठोक्, ठेल् आदि धातु कुन भाषिक स्रोतबाट आएका हुन् भन्नेबारे अहिलेसम्म पनि स्पष्ट हुन सकेको छैन । घुराउ, लड्खडाउ, गम् (विचार गर्नु, गम्नु अर्थ भएको) जस्ता धातु चाहिं नेपालीमा हिन्दी लगायतका आगन्तुक स्रोतबाट आएका हुन् । यस्ता चार स्रोत (कतै पाँच स्रोतको पनि चर्चा पाइने) का धातुहरूको निर्मितिमा बनेका नेपाली समापिका क्रियाहरूको कुल सङ्ख्या करिब १७ लाख छ भनी अनुसन्धाता लोकमणि पौडेलले क्रियापद (२०७६) नाउँको पुस्तकमा उल्लेख गरेका छन् । नेपाली धातुका स्वरूपमात्र नभएर अर्थ पनि संस्कृत धातुसँग दुरुस्त मिल्ने उदाहरण नेपाली परम्परामा प्रशस्त पाइन्छन् । संस्कृतबाट प्राकृत र अपभ्रंश हुँदै नेपालीमा आइपुग्दा कतिपय धातुका अर्थमा अंशतः परिवर्तन भएका पनि देखिन्छन्, यसरी अर्थादेश, अर्थविस्तार, अर्थसङ्कोच, अर्थोत्कर्षर अर्थापकर्ष भएका नेपाली धातुहरू भाषा तथा वाङ्मयमा धेरै नै प्रयोग अवस्थामा छन् । तसर्थ नेपाली धातुरचनामा संस्कृत धातुहरूको प्रत्यक्ष प्रभाव देख्न सकिन्छ ।
american_english: In the present article, how many dhatus have come to be used in the Nepali language from the Sanskrit source (tatsama and tadbhava) of Nepali dhatu-formation? The question of what such dhatus are has been taken up. In this process, chiefly the influence of Sanskrit dhatus on Nepali dhatu-formation, the similarities and dissimilarities obtaining in Sanskrit and Nepali dhatus, have been presented and, by analyzing them, conclusions have been drawn. Here the basis for subject analysis is taken to be Sanskrit's 'Paniniya Dhatupatha' and, for Nepali, the dhatu form (dhatus to which -nu can be added) determined from traditional Nepali grammar. On these very bases, the subject has been analyzed by comparative and descriptive methods. A verb formed by attaching various affixes to a dhatu expresses various tenses and aspects, mood, voice, durativity and the like; therefore the dhatu is the fundamental basis of the meaning conveyed by a verb. When a tense-indicating affix is added to this fundamental meaning of the dhatu, a tense-indicating verb is formed, and when a mood-indicating affix is added, a mood-indicating verb is formed. In this way the structure of other verbs is also formed. Thus the meaning given by a verb is only tense and its aspects, mood, voice, durativity and the like. Since the dhatu before combining with an affix bears and nourishes the determined meaning, the dhatu's meaning of bearing and nourishing (dhiyate'rthah yasmin sa dhatuh) is meaningful. Although there is hardly any problem in the tatsama dhatus used in Nepali, much doubt is seen in many places in tadbhava dhatus. In the process of partial change forming Nepali dhatus, problems of diversity relating to similarity and proximity are seen, such as: in some places it is claimed that many tadbhava dhatus were formed from a single Sanskrit dhatu; in some places it is said that only one Nepali dhatu was formed from a single Sanskrit dhatu; in some places the Sanskrit source is asserted to be this one on the basis of seeking to match the form of the Nepali dhatu, and so on. As examples, chad, di, ughar, dau, ghusar, milau, chun, kat and the like can be taken. Among such dhatus, the Sanskrit source of some is considered investigable, doubtful and disputed, yet they are treated as tadbhava dhatus by the majority. The third-class dhatus in use in Nepali are onomatopoeic; khanakhanaau, gadagadaau, tharatharaau, takatakaau and the like are examples of this. As for fourth-class dhatus, some are loanwords and some have an untraceable source; among these, the source of some untraced dhatus is conjectured to be Prakrit and Apabhramsha sources. It has not yet been possible to make clear from which linguistic source dhatus such as atu, chad, tik, thok, thel and the like have come. Dhatus such as ghurau, ladakhadaau, gam (in the sense of 'to consider', 'to ponder') have come into Nepali from Hindi and other loan sources. Researcher Lokamani Poudel has mentioned in his book 'Kriyapad' (2076) that the total number of Nepali finite verbs formed from dhatus of such four sources (mention of five sources is found in some places) is about 17 lakh. Not only the form of Nepali dhatus but also their meaning matches Sanskrit dhatus exactly; examples of this are found in abundance in the Nepali tradition. When Sanskrit reaches Nepali via Prakrit and Apabhramsha, the meaning of some dhatus is seen to have changed partially; thus Nepali dhatus that have undergone meaning-change (arthadesh, arthavistar, arthasankocha, arthotkarsha and arthapakarsha) are in a state of very frequent use in language and literature. Therefore a direct influence of Sanskrit dhatus can be seen in Nepali dhatu-formation.

informal_english: In this article I'm wondering how many dhatus have actually made their way into Nepali from the Sanskrit source (tatsama and tadbhava) of Nepali dhatu-formation. I've taken up the question of what such dhatus are. Along the way the main thing is the influence of Sanskrit dhatus on Nepali dhatu-formation, plus the similarities and differences between Sanskrit and Nepali dhatus, which I've laid out and worked through to draw some conclusions. The basis I've used for the analysis is Sanskrit's 'Paniniya Dhatupatha' on one side and, on the Nepali side, the dhatu form (dhatus you can add -nu to) that traditional Nepali grammar sets out. From there I've compared and described things. A verb built by tacking affixes onto a dhatu carries tense, aspect, mood, voice, durativity and so on, so the dhatu is really the core of what a verb means. Add a tense affix to that core and you get a tense verb, and add a mood affix and you get a mood verb. That's how the rest of the verb structure falls into place. So a verb's meaning comes down to tense and its aspects, mood, voice, durativity and the like. Because the dhatu holds and nourishes the meaning before any affix joins it, the idea of the dhatu as 'bearer and nourisher' (dhiyate'rthah yasmin sa dhatuh) makes sense. Tatsama dhatus in Nepali are mostly trouble-free, but tadbhava dhatus are full of question marks in lots of places. As Nepali dhatus form through partial change, there are all sorts of similarity-and-proximity puzzles: sometimes people claim many tadbhava dhatus came from one Sanskrit dhatu, sometimes only one Nepali dhatu came from one Sanskrit dhatu, and sometimes the Sanskrit source gets pinned down just because the Nepali dhatu's shape seems to match. Examples include chad, di, ughar, dau, ghusar, milau, chun, kat. Some of these have Sanskrit sources that are debatable, doubtful or disputed, but most folks still treat them as tadbhava. Third-class dhatus in Nepali are onomatopoeic, like khanakhanaau, gadagadaau, tharatharaau, takatakaau. Fourth-class ones are a mix of loanwords and ones whose source can't be traced; the untraced ones are guessed to come from Prakrit or Apabhramsha. For dhatus like atu, chad, tik, thok, thel, nobody's been able to pin down the linguistic source yet. Dhatus like ghurau, ladakhadaau, gam (meaning 'to consider', 'to ponder') came into Nepali from Hindi and other borrowed sources. Researcher Lokamani Poudel notes in his book 'Kriyapad' (2076) that the total number of Nepali finite verbs built from dhatus of these four sources (five get mentioned in some places) is about 17 lakh. It's not just the shape of Nepali dhatus that matches Sanskrit dhatus exactly, the meaning does too, and you see plenty of that in the Nepali tradition. As Sanskrit travels into Nepali through Prakrit and Apabhramsha, some dhatus shift meaning a bit, so Nepali dhatus showing meaning-changes (arthadesh, arthavistar, arthasankocha, arthotkarsha and arthapakarsha) are all over the language and literature. So you can see a direct Sanskrit influence on Nepali dhatu-formation.
